title_ar: كون الشخص في أيام عرسه لا يرخص له ذلك التخلف عن الجماعة
title_en: Being in the days of his wedding does not give a man a dispensation to stay away from the congregation
body_ar:
هل كون الشخص في أيام عرسه يرخص له بسبب ذلك في التخلف عن الجمعة والجماعة هل هذا صحيح أو غير صحيح؟

أنه غير صحيح، بل يجب على المسلم أن يشهد الجمعة وأن يعلم الخطر العظيم في التخلف عنها فقد أخرج مسلم في الصحيح من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله (ص) قال: «لقد هممت أن آمر بحطب فيحطب ثم آمر بنار فتوقد ثم أتخلف إلى بيوت قوم يتخلفون عن الجمعة فأحرق عليهم بيوتهم» وكذلك صح عنه (ص) أنه قال: «ألا هل عسى أن يتخذ أحدكم الضبنة على رأس ميلين أو ثلاثة فيتخلف بها عن الجمعة، فمن تخلف عن الجمعة ثلاثا فلا جمع الله شمله ألا ولا دين له ألا ولا أمانة له»، وكذلك صح عنه (ص) أنه قال: «من ترك ثلاث جمع ختم الله على قلبه»، فهذا تحذير شديد من التخلف عن الجمعة وعلى الذي أنعم الله عليه بأن يسر له الأسباب وهيأ له ما كان يرغب فيه من الزواج أو غيره أن لا يجعل ذلك ذريعة لمعصية الله فإن ما عند الله لا ينال بمعصيته، إن من شكر نعمة الله تعالى على الإنسان إذا تزوج وحصن دينه أن يهتم بالصلاة وأن يزداد اهتمامه بها وأن لا يتخلف عن الجمعة ولا عن الجماعة، وليس ذلك عذرا في التخلف عنها.
body_en:
Does a person's being in the days of his wedding give him, on that account, a dispensation to stay away from the Friday prayer and from the congregation? Is this correct or not correct?

It is not correct. Rather, a Muslim is obliged to be present at the Friday prayer and to know the grave danger there is in staying away from it. Muslim recorded in the Ṣaḥīḥ, from the hadith of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, said: "I have resolved to order firewood to be gathered, then to order a fire to be kindled, then to go off to the houses of a people who stay away from the Friday prayer and burn their houses down upon them." It is likewise soundly established from him, upon whom be peace, that he said: "Is it not the case that one of you may take his ḍabnah two or three miles out, and so stay away with it from the Friday prayer? Whoever stays away from the Friday prayer three times, may God not gather his affairs together for him; indeed, he has no religion, and indeed, he has no trustworthiness." And it is likewise soundly established from him, upon whom be peace, that he said: "Whoever abandons three Friday prayers, God sets a seal upon his heart." This is a severe warning against staying away from the Friday prayer. The one upon whom God has bestowed His favour by making the means easy for him, and by preparing for him what he desired of marriage or anything else, must not make that a pretext for disobeying God, for what is with God is not attained by disobeying Him. It is part of giving thanks for God Most High's favour to a man, when he marries and so fortifies his religion, that he give attention to the prayer, and that his attention to it increase, and that he not stay away from the Friday prayer nor from the congregation. That is no excuse for staying away from it.

flags.context: ألا هل عسى أن يتخذ أحدكم الضبنة على رأس ميلين أو ثلاثة فيتخلف بها عن الجمعة
options: his ḍabnah [his flock and household kept at a distance]
flags.note: Ḍabnah is a rare word in the hadith lexicon. The commentators gloss it variously as a man's sheep and goats, as his household and those he supports, or as the two together — a homestead kept out at a distance from the town. The Sheikh does not gloss it. The point of the report does not turn on which is meant: it is that a man settles himself out of reach of the mosque. Option 0 keeps the Arabic with a minimal bracketed gloss rather than choosing between the commentators.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

The Sheikh attributes the first hadith to Muslim expressly and says of the second and third only that they are 'soundly established' (ṣaḥḥa ʿanhu) without naming a collection. Both attributions are preserved exactly as he gives them; no collection has been supplied for the second and third.

'A pretext for disobeying God' renders dharīʿah li-maʿṣiyat Allāh. The word carries an echo of the Maliki principle of blocking the means to harm (sadd al-dharāʾiʿ), though the Sheikh does not invoke the principle by name.
'Fortifies his religion' renders ḥaṣṣana dīnahu, the standard expression for marriage as a safeguard against unlawful relations.
